markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small, falsifiable intervention: test whether an explicit recent-history residual improves the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Its contribution is a controlled diagnostic-to-intervention case study; weighted recent-item scoring is established [5].

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% training negative-win rate versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. This motivates category analysis, without establishing generalization failure. (2) Embedding alignment scores cluster near 0.54–0.56 despite different margins. Geometry alone cannot explain these gaps. (3) User feedback suggests broad affinity and older interests sometimes overwhelm current evidence. Recency remains a hypothesis, not proof of intent or compatibility.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Shuffling motivates sequence-dependence tests [1], while padding and position effects require matched controls [2,3]. Sensitivity alone cannot establish useful dependence. (2) Sampled metrics can reverse model ordering [4]; catalog diagnostics remain auxiliary. (3) FOSSIL already combines historical and recent-item components [5]. SASRec’s tied scoring makes the residual an explicit item-similarity term, with additional embedding gradients [6].

**Framework and directions.** Cross evidence source (latest, recent, older), intervention (identity replacement, order permutation, residual), and outcome (training diagnostic, pinned validation, catalog audit). Three directions follow: calibrated perturbations, controlled recent-interest modeling, and prospective diagnostic validity. The gap is whether diagnostics identify an intervention that beats both baseline and a matched control.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled perturbation calibration: 4/7/4.** Originality: separates confounds, but extends shuffle tests. Potential: supports interpretation, but provides no direct ranking improvement. Difficulty: few architecture changes, but careful matching and state restoration.
- **Recent-history residual: 2/6/5.** Originality: tests a diagnostic hypothesis, but resembles established recent-item models [5]. Potential: offers a reproducible case study, but recent purchases may satisfy rather than renew needs. Difficulty: simple pooling, but scale, causality, gradients, and serialization require controls.
- **Popularity-mixed negatives: 3/6/3.** Originality: stronger competitors, but established sampling. Potential: tests weak separation, but may misalign with uniform evaluation candidates [4]. Difficulty: simple sampling, but exclusions and false negatives require care.

**Selected algorithm: controlled recent-history residual.** At each causal prefix, compute SASRec state h and a normalized exp(-lag) mean r of the last five raw nonpadding item embeddings. Add after final LayerNorm: q = h + αr; retain tied scoring and existing loss. Specify no additional residual dropout. Lag means interaction position, not elapsed time; approximately 63.6% weight falls on the latest item when five exist, requiring a last-item control.

Pseudocode: `h = SASRec(prefix); r = causal_pool(prefix); q = h + alpha*r; optimize(existing_loss(score(q)))`.

Prespecify baseline, last-item, uniform-five, exponential-five, and exponential-five with shuffled preceding-four residual positions. Keep SASRec input unchanged in the shuffle arm. Use α=0.1 for primary comparisons; retain α∈{0,0.1,0.3} as a declared search space, with 0.3 secondary only if budget permits. Register predictions, minimum gain, failure criteria, checkpoint rules, and stopping rules before training. Match seeds, updates, branch handling, and candidates; report actual compute. Compare exponential pooling against baseline and shuffled control; last-only and uniform isolate additional-history and recency effects. One case study cannot establish general diagnostic validity.

Track norm ratios, alignment, and logit spread; these distinguish possible scale shortcuts from evidence use. Paired category-stratified bootstrap intervals describe conditional user uncertainty, excluding adaptive-search and training-seed uncertainty [7]. Freeze selection for host-held-out confirmation. Preserve all four routes, diagnostic hooks, predictor serialization, required unseen-item recommendations, and existing data restrictions. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Test a causal recent-history residual in SASRec through prespecified baseline, last-item, uniform-history, ordered-recency, and matched shuffled-recency comparisons. Treat this as a controlled test of a diagnostic hypothesis rather than a novel pooling architecture.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnosis suggests broad affinity sometimes overwhelms evidence of current interest, but training margins cannot establish that mechanism. Established recent-item models make a residual feasible at 10% progress; matched controls are necessary to distinguish useful older recent evidence, lag assignment, and generic item-similarity effects.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four datasets and routes, and SASREC_EPOCHS from the environment with the applicable default of 200. Write artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer whenever architecture or scoring changes. Use one GPU and log every attempted configuration, including failures, against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not access hidden tests, fetch additional data or pretrained weights, alter splits, or modify host evaluation.

Define the primary architecture precisely: h_t is the existing SASRec output after its final LayerNorm; r_t pools raw shared-table embeddings of at most five nonpadding inputs at positions <=t, with weights exp(-j)/sum(exp(-j)), j=0 for the latest valid item. Both branches predict the existing positive at t+1. Use zero for an empty prefix, alpha=0.1 for primary comparisons, no extra residual dropout, and q_t=h_t+alpha*r_t without another normalization. Preserve the baseline loss, optimizer, batch construction, training updates, and checkpoint schedule. Query direction and norm can both change; LayerNorm is not unit-L2 normalization. Residual gradients enter the shared embedding table, so gains cannot automatically be attributed to improved temporal reasoning.

Primary arms are baseline alpha=0; last-item residual; uniform mean of the same five items; exponential pooling; and a matched shuffled exponential arm. The shuffled arm permutes only the valid preceding four residual items, preserving the latest item, item multiset, sequence length, mask, and unmodified SASRec input. Use a private, logged seed and reproducible per-prefix permutation, with the same procedure at training and inference. Short prefixes with fewer than three valid items cannot identify ordering beyond the latest item; report their counts and analyze eligible histories separately. Last-only and uniform arms are explanatory ablations; neither alone establishes diagnostic specificity. Shuffling controls lag assignment but does not test the broader claim that recent items outperform old items.

Retain alpha values {0,0.1,0.3} as the declared search space, but reserve 0.3 for secondary work after primary contrasts fit within the remaining budget. Estimate arm cost from baseline throughput; reserve time for serialization and diagnostics, and stop at epoch boundaries before the shared budget is exhausted. If matched arms cannot complete the same training schedule, report the comparison as incomplete rather than interpreting unequal-update results. Predeclare validation checkpoints at epochs 20,40,...,200, restricted to the configured epoch limit and including its final epoch; select by macro validation HR@10 with earliest-checkpoint tie breaking. Use the same schedule for all arms. This checkpoint search remains exploratory.

Before training, record the diagnostic prediction: ordered recent pooling will improve macro validation HR@10 over baseline and matched shuffled pooling, with the largest category gain hypothesized for Electronics. Define the operational minimum meaningful macro gain as 0.005 absolute HR@10; this is a declared threshold, not an observed effect. Failure to meet either primary contrast fails the proposed diagnostic-specificity criterion. Report category regressions, history-length strata, and all arm results. Two-sided primary contrasts are exponential-minus-baseline and exponential-minus-shuffled; if inferential p-values are available, apply Holm correction to these two comparisons. Additional contrasts are exploratory. This adjustment does not correct earlier adaptive search.

When the unchanged host exposes per-user validation hits, preserve all arms together in 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples, sampling 200 users with replacement within each category and averaging category differences equally. Use a private seed 42. Report percentile 95% intervals and discordant hit counts. If only aggregate metrics are exposed, mark paired uncertainty unavailable; do not reconstruct outcomes or replace the host evaluator. Intervals condition on checkpoints and fixed candidates and omit training-seed, candidate-sampling, and adaptive-selection uncertainty. Select solely through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, freeze the chosen artifact, and leave confirmation to the host's held-out evaluation.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module; expose the actual residual-enhanced states through log2feats and matching scores through predict_score. Retain item_emb, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility, while treating unavailable fields as unavailable. Preserve embedding and training-margin probes, sample sizes, finite-value counts, state and RNG restoration, and the distinction between training diagnostics and validation results. Calibrate perturbations with unchanged-input, last-item-only, and history-independent popularity controls. Preserve positions in identity replacements and preserve length, masks, latest item, and multiset in applicable permutations. Report deletion's remaining packing and positional confounds.

Track hidden and residual norms, residual-to-hidden norm ratios, query/item norms, cosine alignment, and logit spread on fixed training prefixes. If primary results justify further work and budget remains, separately test normalized residuals, pre-LayerNorm addition with normalization-only controls, detached residual embeddings, matched training temperature, older-item residuals, and norm-preserving q'=||h||q/(||q||+epsilon). Positive query scaling alone cannot alter a fixed-query ranking, but affects training gradients; these are mechanistic follow-ups, not additional primary search dimensions.

Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for 20 real training users, five per category, and keep these audits auxiliary. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. Do not infer device ownership, functional compatibility, unmet needs, ratings, reviews, item categories/prices/stores, or simulator diversity/conformity traits. A recent-item similarity residual may amplify substitutes, popularity, or repeated-product affinity; it does not directly solve functional complementarity.
idea.pseudocode:
register arms, hypotheses, primary contrasts, checkpoint rules, and budget stop
primary_alpha = 0.1
secondary_alpha_grid = [0.0, 0.1, 0.3]
arms = [baseline, last_only, uniform_five, exponential_five, shuffled_exponential_five]
for arm in arms, subject to the declared budget:
    initialize unchanged SASRec backbone with training seed 42
    for each unchanged training batch and causal position t:
        h_t = backbone.log2feats(sequence)[t]
        ids = last_at_most_five_nonpadding_inputs(sequence, end=t)
        if arm == shuffled_exponential_five:
            ids = reproducibly_permute_earlier_ids_preserving_latest(ids)
        r_t = arm_specific_pool(raw_shared_embeddings(ids))
        q_t = h_t if arm == baseline else h_t + primary_alpha * r_t
        optimize unchanged loss with the existing tied item scorer
    at identical declared checkpoints:
        obtain unchanged host validation results
        select checkpoint by macro HR@10, breaking ties by earlier epoch
    save configuration, checkpoint, and matching predictor
    run compatible diagnostics with complete state restoration
report every attempted arm and category result
compare exponential-minus-baseline and exponential-minus-shuffled
if paired host hits are exposed:
    bootstrap users jointly across arms within categories
    report equal-category macro differences, intervals, and discordant hits
else:
    mark paired uncertainty unavailable
freeze the selected model for independent host-held-out evaluation

originality.positive: Prospectively links a diagnostic observation to a controlled architectural intervention and explicit failure criteria.
originality.negative: Weighted recent-item scoring has strong precedent in FOSSIL and related models; adding it to SASRec supplies limited architectural novelty.

future_potential.positive: A reproducible controlled case study can clarify when history diagnostics identify useful interventions and motivate broader validation.
future_potential.negative: One intervention cannot establish general diagnostic predictive validity, and item similarity does not resolve compatibility, complementarity, or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Pooling and tied scoring require only small model changes and reuse existing embeddings.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal alignment, deterministic matched controls, scale interpretation, diagnostic transactions, predictor reconstruction, and budget-matched comparisons require substantial care.

related_work.title: [1] Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Studies history shuffling in sequential recommendation, motivating direct sequence-dependence tests.
limitations: Sensitivity alone does not establish beneficial dependence or validate the proposed residual.

related_work.title: [2] Repeated Padding
contributions: Shows that padding choices can materially affect sequential recommendation performance.
limitations: Does not separate preference-evidence loss from representation changes in the proposed deletion probes.

related_work.title: [3] CAPE
contributions: Investigates positional encoding choices, supporting controls for item-position assignments.
limitations: Does not establish predictive validity of this diagnostic-to-intervention protocol.

related_work.title: [4] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Demonstrates limitations of sampled recommendation metrics, including possible changes in model ordering.
limitations: Does not identify a winning intervention for this benchmark; the pinned sampled metric remains the required selection objective.

related_work.title: [5] Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: FOSSIL combines a history-based similarity component with weighted recent-item transitions.
Provides direct precedent that lowers the architectural originality of exponential recent-item residuals.
limitations: Its model differs from a SASRec backbone and does not establish the effectiveness of this residual or diagnostic protocol.

related_work.title: [6] SASRec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Makes input embedding scaling, positional embeddings, dropout, final LayerNorm, and tied item scoring explicit.
limitations: A reference implementation cannot establish the exact RecHarness backbone internals; implementation must verify the actual trained module.

related_work.title: [7] The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis
contributions: Establishes the validity problem created by adaptively reusing held-out data, motivating explicit search logs and independent confirmation.
limitations: Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals and correction of only the final contrasts do not remove optimism from preceding adaptive validation search.
